B04-L01 - Operational vs analytical workloads: OLTP and
A transactional database is optimized to record business events safely. An analytical system is optimized to scan, combine and
summarize history. Mixing those jobs carelessly can slow operations and still produce poor analytics.
Classify a workload as operational or analytical, then write the boundary that protects the source while enabling repeatable
Course 1 SQL and business-analysis skills. You only need to recognize tables, rows, keys and business questions.
Picture a shop counter and a back-office planning room. The counter must record each sale quickly and correctly. The planning
room asks what happened across millions of sales. Same business, different workload.
online transaction processing; many small reads/writes that run the business
online analytical processing; larger scans/aggregations used to understand the business
the operational system where business events are first recorded
queries designed for history, comparison, aggregation and decision support
Optional visual: Alex The Analyst, Database vs Data Warehouse vs Data Lake, 00:00-05:22. After watching, write one OLTP and
one OLAP example from the same business. Current reference: Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse.
What you already know as an analyst: You already know how to query tables and answer business questions.
What changes in engineering: In engineering, you must protect the operational source and decide where analytical work should run.
Why engineers care: Heavy scans or uncontrolled transformations on a production source can hurt the system customers depend on.
Small worked example: Ride booking INSERT/update is OLTP. Monthly city revenue by driver cohort is OLAP.
Real engineering version: C3 will build bounded extraction and landing patterns; this lesson only establishes why the boundary
Open B04_WAREHOUSING_DATA_QUALITY_PRACTICE_RC1.xlsx -> Workload_Contract. Classify six Urban Mobility
activities, then write one source-protection rule for each analytical request.
Operational actions favor small, current, keyed transactions. Analytical requests favor historical scans, joins, aggregations and

Calling every SQL database a warehouse; running dashboard-style full scans directly on the app database; treating OLTP/OLAP
Ask: is this action recording/changing one business event now, or summarizing many events to make a decision? Then identify
who is harmed if the query is slow.
For a clinic, classify appointment booking, payment capture, weekly no-show analysis and annual provider-capacity planning.
Every row has workload type + reason + source-risk note. At least one analytical request has an explicit "do not run directly on
Explain OLTP vs OLAP in 60-90 seconds without using the words "small" and "big" as your only reason.

Saved Workload_Contract attempt + changed-domain retry + source-protection rule + own-words explanation. PASS -> B04-L02;

B04-L02 - Warehouse, lake and lakehouse mental models
Engineers choose storage/serving patterns by workload, structure, governance and consumers. Memorizing three definitions is
not enough; a poor fit can create expensive duplication or an ungoverned data swamp.
Choose among warehouse, lake and lakehouse mental models for a stated need and defend one rejected alternative.
B04-L01. No cloud account or platform implementation is required.
Imagine three storage rooms: a labeled reporting room, a flexible raw-material warehouse, and a flexible warehouse with a
managed catalog/table layer on top. The point is not which is "best"; it is which contract fits the work.
structured analytical store optimized for governed SQL/BI workloads
low-cost flexible storage for raw/varied data, usually files/object storage
lake-style storage plus table/management capabilities for reliable analytics
structure is interpreted when data is read
Book-led visual in this lesson: use the three-column decision matrix. Current references: Fabric Data Warehouse and IBM
comparison. The prior IBM video remains audit-history backup only because an exact useful segment was not independently
What you already know as an analyst: You already know structured tables are convenient for BI.
What changes in engineering: Engineering adds raw-data retention, varied formats, governance, cost and multi-workload decisions.
Why engineers care: A reporting-friendly schema and a raw-history store solve different problems; forcing one to do everything
Small worked example: Curated monthly sales mart -> warehouse fit. Raw JSON clickstream archive -> lake fit. Unified table layer
over object storage for BI + engineering -> lakehouse fit.
Real engineering version: C3-04 later implements lakehouse/table-format concepts. B04 only teaches the decision model.
Open Storage_Fit. For each Urban Mobility scenario, choose warehouse/lake/lakehouse and state structure, consumer,
governance and replay needs before choosing.
Different scenarios can reasonably choose different patterns. Your decision cites requirements, not popularity.

Calling a folder of CSVs a governed lakehouse; assuming a lake is automatically cheaper overall; choosing a warehouse for raw
Write four questions: What data shape? Who queries it? How much governance/transaction reliability? Must raw history remain
Choose storage fits for: raw IoT logs, finance reporting mart, and mixed ML + BI history. Reject one alternative for each.
Every decision names at least three requirements and one trade-off; one rejected alternative is defended.
Explain why lakehouse is not simply "warehouse + lake" as a marketing slogan.
Attempt -> protected Review B04-L02 -> close review -> redo with an e-commerce scenario containing images, orders and
Storage_Fit decisions + rejected alternatives + changed retry + own-words explanation. PASS -> B04-L03.

B04-L03 - Business keys, surrogate keys and SCD history
Analysts often receive a clean dimension table. Engineers must decide how source identities and changing descriptive history will
be represented without rewriting the past.
Distinguish business and surrogate keys, choose Type 1 vs Type 2 history behavior, and define effective-date rules at a
B03 grain/key contracts. No SCD implementation code is expected yet.
A provider keeps the same employee number but changes clinic and specialty over time. The source identity is one person; the
warehouse may need multiple historical versions so an old appointment still sees the old context.
identifier supplied by the source/business, such as provider_id
warehouse-generated identifier for a dimension row/version
slowly changing dimension; a pattern for handling descriptive changes
overwrite current descriptive value; no history retained
create a new dimension version and preserve prior history
start/end rules describing when a version is valid
Official references: Dimensional modeling overview and Load tables in a dimensional model. Book-led worked timeline is the
What you already know as an analyst: You already know a dimension needs a usable key.
What changes in engineering: Engineering decides what identity comes from the source, what warehouse key represents a version,
and whether a change rewrites or preserves history.
Why engineers care: Without history rules, last year's facts can suddenly inherit today's customer/provider attributes.
Small worked example: provider_id=P07 remains the business key. City correction typo -> Type 1. Provider changes clinic on
2026-04-01 and history matters -> Type 2 version with a new surrogate key.
Real engineering version: C3-02 later implements snapshots/SCD and late-dimension behavior. Here you must be able to design
Open History_Keys. Inspect driver_profile_changes. Choose Type 1/Type 2 behavior for each attribute, then write a conceptual
surrogate/effective-date strategy and the rule for duplicate effective-date rows.
You separate identity from version. A Type 2 history table can contain multiple rows for one business key but never ambiguous
overlapping active versions under the declared rule.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B04 Warehousing & Data Quality Foundations | INTERNAL QA RC1
The timeline makes historical truth explicit. Facts can later resolve to the correct version by event date rather than today's
Using a business key as if it uniquely identifies every historical version; Type 2 for every typo; overlapping effective intervals;
Ask whether the old value must remain historically true. If yes, history likely matters. Then state the source identity separately
Design history for a customer segment change, corrected spelling, and store-region reassignment.
Business key stated; history choice justified per attribute; no ambiguous active interval; duplicate change trap is surfaced rather
Explain why a surrogate key does not replace the business key's business meaning.
Attempt -> Review B04-L03 -> close -> changed clinic provider-history case with different effective dates.
History_Keys design + one Type 1 and one Type 2 justification + ambiguity check + changed retry. PASS -> B04-L04.

B04-L04 - ETL vs ELT and transformation boundaries
ETL and ELT differ mainly in where durable raw data lands relative to transformation. That boundary affects replay, governance,
compute, debugging and how safely rules can change.
Draw ETL, ELT and hybrid flows and choose where validation/transformation should occur for a stated constraint.
B04-L01-L03. You do not need dbt, orchestration or cloud implementation yet.
ETL is inspect/prepare before the main destination. ELT is land first, then transform inside/near the analytical platform. A hybrid
can still block unsafe fields before landing while retaining replayable raw data where allowed.
clean, standardize, join, derive or reshape data
durable early copy of source data/metadata
the place where business/quality logic is allowed to change data
Optional visual: Kahan Data Solutions, ETL vs ELT - Modern Data Architectures, 00:36-03:19 (ETL 00:36; ELT 01:38;
comparison/trade-off begins 03:19). After watching: close it, draw both three-step arrows, and mark where raw data first becomes
durable. Official reference: Microsoft load-tables guidance.
What you already know as an analyst: You already transform data in Power Query, SQL or pandas.
What changes in engineering: Engineering chooses the durable landing point, transformation boundary and recovery contract
Why engineers care: If a bad transformation overwrites the only copy, replay becomes difficult or impossible.
Small worked example: ELT: source -> raw landing -> warehouse transformation -> mart. ETL: source -> controlled transform ->
curated warehouse. Hybrid: sensitive-field validation/redaction before durable landing plus later analytical transformations.
Real engineering version: C3-01 builds landing/replay; C3-02 implements transformation layers and dbt. B04 only makes the
Open Transform_Boundaries. Draw ETL and ELT for rides + payments. Choose one hybrid constraint and state which data
Your diagram distinguishes source, durable landing/staging, transformation step and curated consumer output.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B04 Warehousing & Data Quality Foundations | INTERNAL QA RC1
A named boundary separates raw evidence from business logic. That makes change/recovery reasoning possible.
Saying ELT means "no cleaning"; calling every sequence ETL; transforming raw evidence in place; assuming cloud always means
Mark the first durable copy. Then ask: if tomorrow's rule changes, what can I replay without requesting the source again?
Design ETL/ELT/hybrid for daily banking transactions with one sensitive field and a monthly reporting mart.
Flow has explicit source, durable point, transform boundary, curated output and replay statement.
Explain ETL vs ELT using where transformation happens relative to durable load, not just the letter order.
Attempt -> Review B04-L04 -> close -> changed subscription-billing flow.
Two flow diagrams + one chosen architecture + replay rationale + changed retry. PASS -> B04-L05.

B04-L05 - Layered analytical systems: raw, staged,
Layers are useful only when each has a clear contract. Naming folders Bronze/Silver/Gold without defining allowed
transformations, consumers and quality gates creates decorative architecture rather than reliability.
Define raw, staged/conformed and serving layer contracts with allowed changes, consumer expectations and quality gates.
B04-L04. No Fabric tenant is required.
Think of evidence -> preparation -> trusted product. Raw preserves what arrived. Staged/conformed normalizes and integrates.
Serving/gold exposes stable business-ready models to consumers.
source-faithful landed data plus ingestion metadata
shared definitions/keys used consistently across subject areas
what may enter, what transformations are allowed, who consumes it, and what quality must pass
Optional visual: Microsoft Learn Together, Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture, 10:09-30:32. After watching,
define allowed state + consumer + quality gate for raw/silver/gold. Current reference: Fabric medallion architecture.
What you already know as an analyst: You already clean raw data and publish a report-ready result.
What changes in engineering: Engineering makes intermediate states explicit, reproducible and owned instead of hiding all steps
Why engineers care: Clear layer contracts make debugging, lineage, testing and replay localizable.
Small worked example: Raw rides keeps source columns + load metadata. Staged rides types timestamps and flags invalid keys.
Conformed aligns rider/driver definitions. Serving exposes monthly_city_metrics at its declared grain.
Real engineering version: C3 later implements these layers with actual files/tables/models; B04 teaches the contract each layer must
Open Layer_Contracts. Place each Urban Mobility source and derived output into a layer. For each layer write allowed changes,
Raw stays recoverable; quality problems can be quarantined/flagged without pretending they never existed; serving outputs have
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B04 Warehousing & Data Quality Foundations | INTERNAL QA RC1
Each transformation belongs to a named stage with an owner and validation point, so failures can be isolated.
Editing raw source rows; putting business KPIs into raw; using layer names with no consumer/quality contract; assuming every
project needs exactly three physical layers.
For each layer answer: what can enter, what may change, who trusts it, and what blocks promotion?
Define layers for support tickets + ticket events + daily team SLA metrics.
Every layer has allowed state, transformation boundary, consumer, quality gate and recoverability statement.
Explain why "Bronze/Silver/Gold" labels alone do not create a medallion architecture.
Attempt -> Review B04-L05 -> close -> changed logistics flow.
Layer_Contracts map + one rejected misplaced transformation + changed retry. PASS -> B04-L06.

B04-L06 - Batch, micro-batch and streaming trade-offs
Faster is not automatically better. Latency choice changes complexity, cost, ordering, late-data handling, replay and operational
Choose batch, micro-batch or streaming from business SLA and failure/replay needs, not from tool popularity.
B04-L05. Kafka or stream-processing code is explicitly not required.
Batch is a scheduled truck carrying many records. Micro-batch is a smaller truck every few minutes. Streaming is a conveyor belt
of events. All can fail; each needs a replay strategy.
delay between an event occurring and being available to the consumer
process a bounded collection on a schedule
continuously process events as they arrive
events arriving after the expected processing window
agreed service expectation, such as freshness or recovery time
Book-led latency/replay decision matrix. Current reference: Fabric data movement decision guide. No external video is required
What you already know as an analyst: You already know a dashboard can refresh daily or more often.
What changes in engineering: Engineering must connect freshness requirements to ingestion mode, event ordering, state, cost and
Why engineers care: Unnecessary real-time design adds failure modes; insufficient freshness can make a system useless.
Small worked example: Daily finance close -> batch. Five-minute operations board -> micro-batch. Fraud/event response requiring
Real engineering version: C3-06 later teaches Kafka/streaming implementation; B04 only establishes when that complexity is
Open Latency_Plan. For four Urban Mobility consumers, write required freshness, volume/burst, late-data tolerance, replay need
At least one case stays batch because its SLA does not justify streaming complexity.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B04 Warehousing & Data Quality Foundations | INTERNAL QA RC1
The business SLA sets the target. Architecture follows the target plus failure/recovery needs.
Choosing streaming because it sounds advanced; confusing refresh frequency with source event time; ignoring late data;
Start with "How stale can this safely be?" Then ask what happens if processing stops for 20 minutes.
Choose modes for payroll, ride-location alerts and hourly marketplace inventory.
Each mode has SLA + late-data + replay + cost/complexity rationale.
Explain a case where batch is more professional than streaming.
Attempt -> Review B04-L06 -> close -> changed hospital operations scenario.
Latency_Plan + one explicit non-streaming decision + changed retry. PASS -> B04-L07.

B04-L07 - Lineage, metadata, ownership and observability
When a number is wrong, an engineer must know where it came from, which step changed it, who owns the issue and what
Create a simple lineage chain and minimum run metadata/ownership contract that supports impact analysis and diagnosis.
B04-L05-L06. No observability platform is required.
Lineage is a map from source to consumer. Metadata is the labels and run evidence on that map. Ownership tells you who can
act when a road is blocked.
data about data/run state, such as source, schema, timestamp and row count
identifier tying logs/evidence to one execution
person/team accountable for a dataset or system boundary
ability to infer system health from evidence such as freshness, volume, errors and logs
Current reference: Microsoft Fabric lineage. Book-led lineage diagram is sufficient; no external video is required.
What you already know as an analyst: You already cite sources and validate outputs.
What changes in engineering: Engineering records dependencies and run evidence systematically so another person can trace
Why engineers care: Without lineage and ownership, a bad source column can silently affect many downstream tables/reports and
nobody knows who should repair it.
Small worked example: rides.csv -> raw_rides -> staged_rides -> monthly_city_metrics -> operations dashboard. Run metadata
stores run_id, source file, ingest time, row count, schema version, status and error count.
Real engineering version: C3-02/C3-08 later implement documentation, tests and observability patterns. B04 defines the minimum
Open Lineage_Ownership. Draw one Urban Mobility lineage chain and fill owner, SLA, run metadata and impact response for
You can answer "what upstream input could have caused this?" and "what downstream consumers are affected?" without opening
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B04 Warehousing & Data Quality Foundations | INTERNAL QA RC1
Dependencies plus run evidence convert debugging from memory into traceable investigation.
Treating a folder path as complete lineage; collecting logs with no run ID; naming an owner with no responsibility boundary;
tracking only failures and not normal row/freshness evidence.
Start from the wrong output and walk upstream one transformation at a time. Write the minimum evidence you would need at each
Build lineage for clinic appointments -> cleaned appointments -> provider utilization -> dashboard.
Chain has upstream/downstream links, owner, freshness expectation, run ID evidence and one failure-impact route.
Explain the difference between lineage and logging.
Attempt -> Review B04-L07 -> close -> changed subscription pipeline lineage.
Lineage diagram + metadata contract + ownership/impact note + changed retry. PASS -> B04-L08.

B04-L08 - Data-quality contracts: block, warn and reconcile
Data quality is not "clean everything." Engineers decide which failures block publication, which can be warned/quarantined, what
gets reconciled and who owns the decision.
Write a data-quality contract with rule, severity, action, owner, evidence and independent reconciliation.
B04-L03 and B04-L07. You already know analyst-side quality checks from Course 1.
Imagine airport security: some conditions stop the passenger, some trigger secondary screening, some are recorded for
follow-up. The action depends on risk, not whether the check is easy.
declared rule + expected result + severity + action + owner + evidence
stop promotion/publish because correctness is unsafe
independent comparison proving counts/totals/keys across boundaries
defect that invalidates trustworthy use until resolved
Current reference: Microsoft dimensional load guidance. Book-led severity matrix is the primary visual.
What you already know as an analyst: You already check duplicates, nulls, types, keys and totals.
What changes in engineering: Engineering turns those checks into reusable contracts with severity, pipeline action, ownership and
Why engineers care: A check that finds a problem but does not define what happens next is not an operational control.
Small worked example: Duplicate driver history effective-date pair -> BLOCK history promotion. One orphan event with preserved
raw evidence -> QUARANTINE + WARN depending consumer contract. Payment total mismatch -> BLOCK serving publication until
Real engineering version: C3-01/C3-02/C3-08 later implement automated tests/quarantine/observability. B04 establishes the
Open Quality_Contract. Define six Urban Mobility checks spanning required key, duplicate history, orphan FK, type/business rule,
Every check has expected result, severity, action, owner and saved evidence. Not every defect is silently dropped.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B04 Warehousing & Data Quality Foundations | INTERNAL QA RC1
Severity links technical evidence to business risk. Independent reconciliation catches failures that a single row-level rule can miss.
Replacing errors with zero; deleting orphans to make counts match; marking every issue BLOCK; using one grand total as proof
For each defect ask: can a consumer make a materially wrong decision if this passes? If yes, block or isolate until explicitly
Write quality contracts for clinic appointment IDs, payment totals, provider history and late events.
At least one BLOCK, one WARN/QUARANTINE, one independent reconciliation and named owner. No issue is hidden by
Explain why "0 errors" can be less trustworthy than an explicit quarantine count.
Attempt -> Review B04-L08 -> close -> changed marketplace quality case.
Quality_Contract + severity rationale + reconciliation + changed retry. PASS -> B04-L09.
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B04 Warehousing & Data Quality Foundations | INTERNAL QA RC1
B04-L09 - Replay, backfill and warehouse failure-recovery
A professional pipeline is not proven by one successful run. You need to know how to recover from bad logic, missing periods or
partial failure without corrupting trusted outputs.
Write a conceptual replay/backfill runbook that preserves raw evidence, isolates scope, protects live state and proves correctness
B04-L04-L08. Implementation of checkpoints/orchestration belongs to C3.
Think of a damaged chapter in a printed ledger. You do not rewrite the entire archive from memory. You identify the affected
pages, return to preserved evidence, reprocess a bounded range, compare controls, and only then republish.
run processing again from preserved input/state
process a historical period that was missed or needs rebuilding
rerunning safely produces the intended state without accidental duplication
reprocess only a declared scope/window with controlled state
independent proof the repaired result is complete and not duplicated
Book-led recovery sequence. Current reference: Fabric medallion architecture for preserved raw/layered reasoning. No external
What you already know as an analyst: You already rerun a notebook or refresh a report when something changes.
What changes in engineering: Engineering makes rerun scope, durable inputs, state protection, duplicate prevention and
Why engineers care: Blind reruns can double-count facts, overwrite history or advance state before completeness is proven.
Small worked example: Bad transformation affected rides for 2026-03-01. Freeze serving output, identify affected window, replay
from preserved raw, write to isolated candidate, reconcile rows/payment total, compare keys, then promote and record run evidence.
Real engineering version: C3-01 implements state/replay/backfill and C3-00/C3-03 deepen idempotence/runbooks/orchestration.
B04 must prepare the reasoning without hiding those prerequisites.
Open Recovery_Runbook. Use an Urban Mobility failure scenario: one day of rides loaded but payment reconciliation failed. Write
detect -> contain -> scope -> replay -> validate -> promote -> document.
State is not advanced simply because part of the run succeeded. Raw evidence stays unchanged. Promotion occurs only after
C2B DA-to-DE Bridge | B04 Warehousing & Data Quality Foundations | INTERNAL QA RC1
Bounded recovery separates diagnosis, reprocessing and promotion. It prevents "rerun everything and hope" behavior.
Deleting bad output before preserving evidence; advancing checkpoint before reconciliation; rerunning unbounded history;
validating only the metric that originally failed.
Write seven verbs in order: detect, contain, identify scope, recover from preserved input, validate independently, promote,
Write a backfill plan for two missing days of support-ticket events when daily SLA aggregates already exist.
Runbook names affected window, source evidence, state/checkpoint handling, duplicate prevention, at least two independent
Explain the difference between replay and backfill and why both need post-recovery validation.
Attempt -> Review B04-L09 -> close -> changed CareFlow payment/orphan-event recovery case.
Recovery runbook + bounded scope + independent controls + changed retry. PASS -> independent CareFlow Mini-Lab; after

C2B / B04 / ASTRA PARITY RC4
B04 Quick Revision
Warehouse boundaries, history, quality and recovery
C2B / B04 / CHECKPOINT44
Page 1
Closed-book revision map
Lesson
Recall contract
B04-L01
Separate OLTP event recording from OLAP historical decision workloads; protect the operational
source.
B04-L02
Choose warehouse/lake/lakehouse from data shape, governance, consumer and replay needs, not
product branding.
B04-L03
Separate business identity from warehouse version identity; SCD history cannot have ambiguous
effective intervals.
B04-L04
Name durable landing and transformation boundary; raw evidence must remain replayable.
B04-L05
Layer contracts define allowed state, transformations, consumers and promotion gates.
B04-L06
Choose batch/micro-batch/streaming from SLA, late-data and replay trade-offs.
B04-L07
Lineage + metadata + ownership must make impact and freshness explainable.
B04-L08
Quality rules need severity, owner and block/warn/reconcile action.
B04-L09
Replay/backfill must be bounded, idempotent where required and must not mutate raw evidence.
Failure-first recall
- Inventory and other snapshot measures are semi-additive across time: summing daily snapshots can
create a believable but meaningless total.
- A current-master row is not a historical truth table. Same-day conflicting changes are a blocker until
resolved.
- Orphan records must remain visible as quality evidence; deleting them to make joins clean is a critical
failure.
- Many-to-many tags/memberships can multiply transaction measures if joined before aggregation.
- Higher-grain targets belong at their own grain; compare only after actuals are aggregated compatibly.
- Replay is safe only when the source slice, watermark/window, transformation version, destination
behavior and reconciliation are explicit.
Move on when
With the book closed, you can classify workload/storage/layers, design history, state latency and lineage
contracts, define block/warn quality rules, and explain a bounded replay plan with independent
reconciliation.

B04 Practical Mastery Check
Closed-book warehouse and quality transfer - non-gating
C2B / B04 / CHECKPOINT44
Page 1
Non-gating closed-book mastery check
This mastery check never unlocks or blocks Gate A. Save a genuine attempt before opening its
protected review.
Scenario - Urban Mobility analytical platform
- Classify booking/payment operations vs historical analytics and write one source-protection boundary.
- Choose a storage/serving pattern for raw ride events, conformed ride facts and governed KPI outputs;
state one rejected alternative.
- Design driver history: state business key, warehouse version key, Type 1 vs Type 2 attributes and what
makes an effective interval invalid.
- Draw source -> durable landing -> staged/conformed -> serving layers and name the quality gate
between each trusted state.
- Choose batch, micro-batch or streaming for three flows with explicit freshness, late-data and replay
reasoning.
- Write lineage/ownership metadata for one KPI from source through transform to consumer.
- Define at least six quality rules with severity and action. Include duplicate history, orphan FK, row-count
reconciliation and amount reconciliation.
- Write a bounded backfill plan that preserves raw evidence and prevents double publish.

C2B / B04 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT44
Page 2
Evidence to save before review
- Architecture/layer sketch.
- History/SCD decision table.
- Quality contract with block/warn/reconcile actions.
- Latency plan and late-data rule.
- Lineage chain with owner.
- Replay/backfill runbook and reconciliation evidence.
- One rejected design with reason.
Pass standard
The check is mastered only when the design is internally consistent, independent controls reconcile, and
you can explain which failures block promotion. A polished architecture diagram alone is not a pass.

failure-recovery reasoning

document.

Why plausible output can still be wrong
- seller_tags is legitimate membership data, but joining it before GMV aggregation multiplies transaction
value.
- The S008 same-day conflicting history rows create ambiguous as-of truth and must block historical
attribution until resolved.
- The orphan payout must remain visible in the quality exception path; matched payout total is 163680.00
and orphan amount is 500.00.
- Category targets are month-category grain. Beauty has targets even though completed Beauty GMV is
zero, so missing/zero actual must not be silently dropped.

C2B / B04 / ASTRA PARITY RC4 / CHECKPOINT44
Page 2
Reasoning and evidence rubric
- State source grain and key before designing joins or layers.
- Separate current master from effective-dated history and reject overlapping/conflicting intervals.
- Name durable raw evidence and the transformation/promotion boundaries.
- Define block, warn and reconcile rules with owners and evidence.
- Predict fan-out/semi-additive risk before aggregating.
- Keep orphans and rejected rows in an auditable exception path.
- Reconcile row counts and business totals independently before trusted promotion.
- For backfill/replay, bound the slice, preserve raw evidence, prevent duplicate publish and prove
reconciliation after rerun.
Critical failures
- Hidden data loss or deleted exception evidence.
- Ambiguous history accepted as truth.
- Snapshot or many-side joins produce inflated but plausible measures.
- Higher-grain targets repeated at transaction grain.
- Unbounded replay or unsafe state advancement.
- No independent reconciliation or ownership.

Page 3

- Keep the original Gate attempt append-only.
- Open only this matching protected review after the saved genuine attempt.
- Repair the named weakness using the targeted remediation cards.
- Close the review and perform a changed micro-proof in a different small scenario.
- Save the retry evidence separately. Gate B/C exposure still requires the existing explicit reassignment
controls.
Next route
PASS with all competency floors and no unresolved critical failure -> B05. Otherwise repair; Gate B
remains sealed.
